piece.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:77, Op.76 No.3 (“Emperor”)
piece.movement: II. Poco adagio; cantabile — Var. II
piece.why: Variation II: the hymn moves to the cello while Violin I plays a busy countermelody above it. Both planners mislabel the violin as the tune here; the cello's hymn is still kept.

plan.summary: As written (no arranging): the original parts are handed out unchanged. The source parts in score order (Violin 1, Violin 2, Viola and Violoncello) are paired with the players sorted from highest to lowest range center (the midpoint of each player's sounding range): Violin 1 → Alto Sax in E♭; Violin 2 → Tenor Sax in B♭; Viola → Baritone Sax in E♭. No octave shifts, no chord changes beyond what a one-note instrument requires (a wind or brass player plays the top note of a double stop or chord), and no repair: a note outside a player's range stays where it is and is marked with an x notehead. There are fewer players than parts, so Violoncello is left out: nobody left to play it.

assignments.reason: as written: Violin 1 goes to Alto Sax in E♭, the highest range center (sounding E♭3–G5); no octave shift, no repair
as written: Violin 2 goes to Tenor Sax in B♭, the 2nd highest range center (sounding B♭2–D5); no octave shift, no repair
as written: Viola goes to Baritone Sax in E♭, the 3rd highest range center (sounding E♭2–G4); no octave shift, no repair
